proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(q=|F|\).  By \(\{s\}\subsetneq F\) in
\(\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\), we have \(q\geq 2\).  For every
\(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), let \(d(v)\) be the length of a shortest
directed path from \(v\) to \(s\) in \(D[F]\), whose existence is part of
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\).  Choose the first edge
\(v\to p(v)\) of such a path.  Then
\[
 d(p(v))=d(v)-1.
\]
Consequently the \(q-1\) chosen unordered pairs are distinct, and iteration
of \(p\) reaches \(s\).  They therefore form a spanning tree of the
underlying undirected graph of \(D[F]\).  Independently, connectivity of
\(B[F]\) gives a bidirected spanning tree and hence at least \(q-1\)
bidirected pairs.  Bow-freeness makes every directed pair distinct from every
bidirected pair.  Simplicity then gives
\[
 2(q-1)\leq \binom q2,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad q\geq4.
\]

Suppose now that \(q=4\).  Equality holds in the preceding display.  Thus
\(D[F]\) has exactly three unordered pairs, \(B[F]\) has exactly three
pairs, both underlying graphs are spanning trees, and their pair sets
partition \(\binom F2\).  A tree on four vertices is either a star or a
path.  The complement of a star has its center isolated, contrary to the
connectivity of the complementary tree.  Hence the directed underlying tree
is a spanning path, and its complement \(B[F]\) is also a spanning path.
Because every vertex reaches \(s\) and an undirected tree has a unique path
to \(s\), every directed edge is oriented along that path toward \(s\).

Conversely, if the directed pairs form a spanning path oriented toward
\(s\), every vertex has a directed path to \(s\); if \(B[F]\) is its
complementary spanning path, then \(B[F]\) is connected.  Together with
\(\{s\}\subsetneq F\), these are exactly the conditions in
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\), so \(F\) is a hedge.

If \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), every
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) is \(F\setminus\{s\}\) for a hedge \(F\), and the
first part gives \(|R|\geq3\).  Therefore \(r(G,s)\leq2\) forces
\(\mathcal C(G,s)=\varnothing\).  Finally, let
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) have size three.  Then
\(F=R\cup\{s\}\) is a four-vertex hedge.  The two complementary paths use
every pair in \(\binom F2\).  Hence for every \(v\in R\), the pair
\(\{v,s\}\) is either bidirected or directed.  In the directed case the
orientation-toward-\(s\) conclusion gives \(v\to s\), so
\(v\in P_s\); in the bidirected case \(v\in T_s\).  Both spanning trees
have positive degree at \(s\), so \(R\) meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\).
The equality \(P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing\) is exactly the bow-free condition
applied to pairs incident to \(s\).  This proves every assertion.

Fix a total order on \(U\).  Order the constructed vertices by putting the
\(x_u\)'s first in the given order, all guards next, and \(s\) last.  Every
directed edge in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}expansion}\)
points forward in this order: \(x_u\to x_v\) has \(u\prec v\), while
\(x_v\to z_e\) and \(z_e\to s\) cross the next two blocks.  Thus \(D\) is
acyclic.  The directed pairs are of the three displayed types, whereas the
bidirected pairs are precisely \(\{s,x_u\}\) and
\(\{x_u,z_e\}\), where \(u\) is the earlier endpoint of \(e\).  These lists
are disjoint, so \(G_H\) is bow-free and simple.

The bidirected graph is connected: every \(x_u\) is adjacent to \(s\), and
every \(z_e\) is adjacent to its designated earlier endpoint \(x_u\).
It has
\[
 |U|+|E|=(1+|U|+|E|)-1
\]
edges, so it is a tree.  Its distance from \(s\) is one at every \(x_u\)
and two at every guard, proving radius at most two (with the evident radius
zero convention when only \(s\) is present).

For an edge \(e=\{u,v\}\) with \(u\prec v\), put
\[
 F_e=\{s,x_u,x_v,z_e\}.
\]
The directed path \(x_u\to x_v\to z_e\to s\) makes every vertex of
\(F_e\) reach \(s\).  The bidirected edges
\(s\leftrightarrow x_u\), \(s\leftrightarrow x_v\), and
\(x_u\leftrightarrow z_e\) connect \(B[F_e]\).  Hence \(F_e\) is a hedge.
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) excludes every
proper hedge with fewer than four vertices, so \(F_e\) is inclusion-minimal
and \(\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\in\mathcal C(G_H,s)\).

For the reverse inclusion, let \(F\) be any hedge in \(G_H\).  Since the
only bidirected neighbors of \(s\) are source-copy vertices and \(B[F]\) is
connected with \(|F|>1\), the set \(F\) contains some \(x_w\).  Choose a
directed path in \(D[F]\) from \(x_w\) to \(s\).  Only guards have an edge
into \(s\), and the unique directed in-neighbor of a guard \(z_e\) is the
later endpoint \(x_v\) of its source edge.  Thus the last two edges of the
chosen path are
\[
 x_v\longrightarrow z_e\longrightarrow s
\]
for a unique \(e=\{u,v\}\) with \(u\prec v\).  The guard \(z_e\) has the
unique bidirected neighbor \(x_u\).  Connectivity of \(B[F]\), together
with \(s,z_e\in F\), therefore forces \(x_u\in F\).  We have proved
\[
 F_e=\{s,x_u,x_v,z_e\}\subseteq F.
\]
It follows that every hedge contains an intended four-vertex hedge.  If
\(F\) is inclusion-minimal, equality must hold.  This proves
\[
 \mathcal C(G_H,s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E\bigr\}.
\]
All members on the right have size three.  Hence the residual rank is three
when \(E\neq\varnothing\).  When \(E=\varnothing\), the reverse-inclusion
argument would associate any hedge with an edge of \(E\), which is
impossible; the clutter is empty and the rank is zero.

As a destructive finite check not used in the proof, an independent
enumerator tested all \(1{,}099\) labeled source graphs on one through five
vertices and all \(1{,}900{,}363\) resulting residual subsets, as well as
all \(32{,}767\) residual subsets for each of \(K_{3,3}\) and the triangular
prism.  Every enumerated hedge contained an intended \(F_e\), and every
intended \(F_e\) satisfied both defining predicates.

By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\), the
constraints of the MCID instance are exactly
\[
 A\cap\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\neq\varnothing,
 \qquad e=\{u,v\}\in E.
\]
If \(C\subseteq U\) is a vertex cover, then
\(A_C=\{x_u:u\in C\}\) meets every displayed triple and, under unit costs,
\(c(A_C)=|C|\).  This gives
\(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\leq\tau(H)\).

Conversely, let \(A\) be feasible.  Start with
\(C_A=\{u:x_u\in A\}\).  For each selected guard \(z_e\in A\) whose edge
\(e=\{u,v\}\) is not yet covered by \(C_A\), insert either endpoint of
\(e\).  Feasibility of \(A\) implies that every edge is then covered: if
neither endpoint copy lies in \(A\), the corresponding constraint forces
\(z_e\in A\).  At most one source vertex is inserted for each selected
guard, and repeated insertions are merged.  Therefore
\[
 |C_A|\leq |A|.
\]
Taking an optimal \(A\) yields \(\tau(H)\leq
\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\), proving equality.

For completeness, consider the standard \(L\)-reduction inequalities.  The
forward map obeys
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)
 \leq 1\cdot\tau(H).
\]
For every feasible \(A\), its replacement cover satisfies
\[
 0\leq |C_A|-\tau(H)
 \leq |A|-\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c).
\]
Thus the two \(L\)-reduction constants are \(\alpha=\beta=1\).  The maps
create \(1+|U|+|E|\) vertices and are polynomial-time maps.  The cited
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cubic\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}apx\mbox{-}complete}\)
states that minimum vertex cover remains \(\mathsf{APX}\)-complete at
maximum degree three; in particular it is both \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and
\(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard there.  The objective-preserving \(L\)-reduction
transfers these two hardness conclusions.  The structural promises in the
claim follow from Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\), independently of
the source degree.

Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every residual in \(\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size at
most three by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\).  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) says that every
nonempty residual has size at least three; hence it has size exactly three,
is contained in the disjoint union \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\), and meets
both parts.

The covering polytope is nonempty because \(y_v=1\) for all
\(v\in V^{-}\) is feasible, and it is compact because it is a closed subset
of \([0,1]^{V^{-}}\).  Thus an optimum \(y\) exists.  Fix
\(0<t<1/2\) and suppose that a residual \(R\) is missed by \(A_t\).  Put
\(a=|R\cap P_s|\).  The preceding paragraph gives \(a\in\{1,2\}\).  Missing
\(R\) means
\[
 y_p<t\quad(p\in R\cap P_s),
 \qquad
 y_b<\tfrac12-t\quad(b\in R\cap T_s).
\]
If \(a=1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v<t+2(\tfrac12-t)=1-t<1;
\]
if \(a=2\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v<2t+(\tfrac12-t)=\tfrac12+t<1.
\]
Both conclusions contradict the LP constraint for \(R\).  Hence every
\(A_t\) is feasible.

Let \(T\) be uniform on \((0,1/2)\).  Direct calculation, using the two
threshold directions, gives
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_p\}\quad(p\in P_s),
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_b\}\quad(b\in T_s).
\]
Vertices outside \(P_s\cup T_s\) are never selected.  Linearity of
expectation and positivity of the costs yield
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{v\in A_T}c(v)\right]
 =\sum_{v\in P_s\cup T_s}c(v)\min\{1,2y_v\}
 \leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 =2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
The incidence vector of every feasible intervention is feasible for the LP,
so
\(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\).

It remains to justify deterministic computation.  Away from the finite set
of critical values
\[
 \{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup
 \{\tfrac12-y_b:b\in T_s\}
\]
inside \((0,1/2)\), the set \(A_t\) is constant on each open cell.  Since
the critical values have Lebesgue measure zero, the expectation inequality
implies that at least one such cell has cost at most
\(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\).  The corrected construction in
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\) evaluates
one rational representative of every cell (and the critical values), hence
finds a set with this bound.  Proposition
\(\mathrm{prop{:}promised\mbox{-}enumeration}\) supplies all constraints in
polynomial time under the rank-three promise; the cited Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) supplies
an optimal rational \(y\) in polynomial time; and sorting and scanning
\(O(|V|)\) rational critical values is polynomial.  This proves the claimed
algorithm and both inequalities.

We prove the narrowed, well-typed statement, restricting the ratio to
instances with \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\).  On such a unit-cost
instance, any \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) gives
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}y_v\geq\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1
\]
for every LP-feasible \(y\); hence \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)>0\), so the
ratio is defined.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\)
then gives
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq2.
\]

For the matching sequence, take \(H=K_n\) with \(n\geq2\) and its
private-guard expansion.  Theorems
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) and
\(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) give the
required bow-free, rank-three, radius-two structure and
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n)=n-1.
\]
The fractional vector \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) is feasible for
every residual triple, so its objective is \(n/2\).  Conversely, summing all
\(\binom n2\) residual constraints and dividing by \(n-1\) gives, for every
feasible \(y\),
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac1{n-1}\sum_{e\in E}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac{\binom n2}{n-1}=\frac n2.
\]
Since \(n\geq2\), the unit-cost objective is at least the left side.  Thus
\(\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=n/2\) and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 {\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
Together with the upper bound, this proves that the supremum is two.

For conditional hardness, suppose for some fixed \(\epsilon>0\) that a
polynomial algorithm achieved factor \(2-\epsilon\) on the stated causal
class.  Given any source graph \(H\) with at least one edge, construct
\(G_H\), run that algorithm, and replace every selected guard by an endpoint
as in the proof of Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\).  The
resulting vertex cover \(C_A\) satisfies
\[
 |C_A|\leq |A|
 \leq(2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
All transformations are polynomial, and edgeless source instances are
trivial.  This contradicts the cited Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\) under
\(\mathsf{UGC}\).  Hence no such causal approximation algorithm exists.

Fix an integer \(r_0\geq0\) and assume the supplied promise
\(r(G,s)\leq r_0\).  Enumerate subsets \(R\subseteq V^{-}\) of size at most
\(r_0\) in lexicographic order.  For each \(R\), put
\(F=R\cup\{s\}\).  Bidirected connectivity of \(B[F]\) is decided by one
graph search.  The condition that every vertex of \(F\) reaches \(s\) in
\(D[F]\) is decided by a reverse directed search from \(s\).  By Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\), these two tests are equivalent
to \(F\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\).

If the hedge test succeeds, test every proper subset \(R'\subsetneq R\) in
the same way.  The set \(R\) is retained exactly when no such \(R'\) is a
hedge residual.  This is equivalent to membership in
\(\mathcal C(G,s)\) by Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\).  Every clutter
member has size at most \(r_0\) by the promise and is therefore tested; no
nonmember is output; and lexicographic subset generation gives exact-once
output.  There are \(O(|V|^{r_0})\) candidates, at most \(2^{r_0}\) proper
subsets per candidate, and each graph search is polynomial.  For fixed
\(r_0\) this is \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\) time.  Streaming the candidates and
retaining only the output list and graph-search workspaces uses polynomial
space.  At \(r_0=3\), Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) excludes smaller
residuals, leaving \(O(|V|^3)\) triple tests and hence the stated bound.

For the cardinality-bounded optimization, first enumerate the clutter under
the rank-three promise.  At a search node with current set \(A_0\) and
remaining budget \(j\), return \(A_0\) if it hits every residual, and fail if
\(j=0\) otherwise.  In the remaining case choose an uncovered residual
\(R\).  It has size three by Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) and the promise, so
branch to \(A_0\cup\{v\}\) for each \(v\in R\), with budget \(j-1\).
Every feasible extension must contain some \(v\in R\), so induction on
\(j\) proves that the recursion retains a least-cost feasible extension of
cardinality at most the original budget whenever one exists.  Positive
costs justify terminating a successful branch immediately, since adding a
vertex cannot lower its cost.  There are at most
\[
 1+3+\cdots+3^k=O(3^k)
\]
nodes.  Each node performs polynomial work on the enumerated clutter, and
rational additions and comparisons have polynomial bit complexity in the
input cost-encoding length \(L\).  This proves the stated runtime and the
scope of the optimum: it is exact only among sets of cardinality at most
\(k\).

Let \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\) denote the family produced by testing every
residual of size at most three.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) proves that every
member is a triple contained in \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\) and meeting
both parts.  Apply the parent--spouse thresholds to an optimum
\(y^{(3)}\) of the LP having only the constraints in
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  If a triple with one parent were missed, its
fractional sum would be strictly less than
\(t+2(1/2-t)=1-t<1\); if a triple with two parents were missed, its sum
would be strictly less than \(2t+(1/2-t)=1/2+t<1\).  Thus every threshold
set hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  Integrating over uniform
\(t\in(0,1/2)\), exactly as in the proved selection-probability calculation
of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\), gives a
candidate hitting set \(A\) satisfying
\[
 c(A)\leq2\operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}
 \leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]
The second inequality holds without a rank promise: every intervention that
hits the full clutter also hits its subfamily \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), so its
incidence vector is feasible for the restricted LP.

Alternatively, let \(A\) be an exact minimum-cost integral hitting set for
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  If the subsequent verification declares \(A\)
globally feasible, then
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq c(A)=\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3},
\]
so \(A\) is globally exact.  If the rounded set is declared feasible, the
first display gives its global factor-two guarantee.  These conclusions use
verification for feasibility, not as evidence that the rank promise holds.

To perform verification, apply Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}hedge\mbox{-}oracle}\) to
\(F_0=V\setminus A\), which contains \(s\).  A fixed point equal to
\(\{s\}\) proves that no hedge avoids \(A\), hence verification succeeds.
Otherwise the lemma returns a hedge \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\).  Minimize
it as follows.  For each \(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), apply the same oracle to
\(F\setminus\{v\}\).  If a hedge survives, replace \(F\) by the returned
fixed-point hedge and restart.  Every replacement strictly decreases
\(|F|\), and every oracle call is polynomial, so the procedure terminates in
polynomial time.

At termination, \(F\) is inclusion-minimal.  Indeed, if a proper hedge
\(J\subsetneq F\) existed, choose
\(v\in F\setminus J\); then the survival property of the fixed-point oracle
would find a hedge in \(F\setminus\{v\}\), contradicting termination.  Thus
\(R=F\setminus\{s\}\) lies in \(\mathcal C(G,s)\).  Since
\(F\subseteq V\setminus A\), this residual is disjoint from \(A\).  But
\(A\) hit every member of \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\); hence \(R\) cannot have
size at most three.  Therefore \(|R|>3\), which is the promised verifiable
rank-violation certificate.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(F\subseteq V\) with \(s\in F\), alternating restriction to the
vertices that reach \(s\) in \(D\) and to the bidirected component of \(s\)
terminates in polynomial time at a fixed set \(F^{\star}\).  The induced
graph on \(F\) contains a member of \(\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\) if and only if
\(F^{\star}\neq\{s\}\); in that case \(F^{\star}\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For \(W\subseteq F\) containing \(s\), define
\[
 \mathsf A(W)=\{v\in W:v\text{ reaches }s\text{ in }D[W]\}
\]
and let \(\mathsf K(W)\) be the vertex set of the connected component of
\(s\) in \(B[W]\).  Starting at \(W_0=F\), alternate
\(W_{2j+1}=\mathsf A(W_{2j})\) and
\(W_{2j+2}=\mathsf K(W_{2j+1})\).  The sequence is decreasing and contains
\(s\) throughout.  Every nonstationary step deletes a vertex, so after at
most \(2|V|\) graph searches it reaches a common fixed point
\(F^{\star}\).

If \(J\subseteq W_i\) is a hedge, its directed paths to \(s\) show that
\(J\subseteq\mathsf A(W_i)\), and its bidirected connectivity shows that
\(J\subseteq\mathsf K(W_i)\).  Induction gives
\(J\subseteq F^{\star}\).  Conversely, at a common fixed point every vertex
reaches \(s\) in \(D[F^{\star}]\), and \(B[F^{\star}]\) is connected.  If
\(F^{\star}\neq\{s\}\), Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) therefore makes it a hedge.  If
\(F^{\star}=\{s\}\), the survival implication excludes any hedge in the
original \(F\).  Each restriction is a directed or undirected graph search,
which proves polynomial runtime.

added_lemmas.statement: Minimum Vertex Cover on graphs of maximum degree at most three is \(\mathsf{APX}\)-complete.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\)
over unit-cost bow-free singleton instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\),
\(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), and radius-two bidirected trees equals
two. For \(G_{K_n}\) with \(n\geq2\), the ratio is \(2-2/n\). Under
\(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time
\((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on this same promised-rank class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The displayed ratio is undefined on hedge-free instances, where both the integral and fractional optima are zero. Restricting the supremum to nonempty clutters makes the division well typed and leaves the claimed upper bound, complete-graph sequence, and conditional hardness frontier unchanged.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Given an optimal fractional solution \(y\), form the critical values
\(\{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup\{1/2-y_b:b\in T_s\}\) that lie in \((0,1/2)\).
These values partition \((0,1/2)\) into finitely many open cells.  Evaluate
\(A_t=\{p\in P_s:y_p\geq t\}\cup\{b\in T_s:y_b\geq1/2-t\}\) at every
critical value and at one rational representative of every nonempty open
cell, and return a cheapest evaluated set.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The expectation argument guarantees a cheap threshold on a positive-measure open cell, not necessarily at a measure-zero critical value. Evaluating one rational representative of every cell is the finite deterministic scan that the proof actually certifies.

proposed.statement:
Assign unit cost to every vertex of \(G_H\). Every vertex cover
\(C\subseteq U\) maps to the intervention \(\{x_u:u\in C\}\) with the same
cost, and every feasible intervention maps in polynomial time, by replacing
each selected \(z_e\) with an endpoint of \(e\), to a vertex cover of no
larger cost. Therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\). The
reduction is an \(L\)-reduction with constants one, so rank-three MCID is
\(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard even with unit costs and a
radius-two bidirected tree; the \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness remains for source
graphs of maximum degree three.
proposed.justification: Objective preservation identifies the exact complexity transition at the first nonempty rank rather than importing generic three-hitting-set hardness.
proposed.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove unrestricted MCID hardness, while Alimonti and Kann supply cubic vertex-cover hardness; neither gives a promise-preserving rank-three causal realization.
proposed.consumer: The result supplies structured hard instances on which the RC2 and Gurobi formulations can be evaluated without uncontrolled hedge rank.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the theorem-granularity published hardness leaf used by the proof.

proposed.statement:
Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size
three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the
natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and
some breakpoint choice satisfies
\(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq
2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time
after promised-rank enumeration.
proposed.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
proposed.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
proposed.consumer: The theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the theorem-granularity rational linear-programming result used for the polynomial runtime claim; the proof uses the corrected finite threshold scan.

proposed.statement:
The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\)
over unit-cost bow-free singleton instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\),
\(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\), and radius-two bidirected trees equals
two. For \(G_{K_n}\) with \(n\geq2\), the ratio is \(2-2/n\). Under
\(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time
\((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on this same promised-rank class.
proposed.justification: A matching gap family and conditional lower bound certify that factor two is the exact polynomial frontier under the standard conjecture.
proposed.gap: Khot and Regev establish the threshold for vertex cover, and Singh characterizes the source LP gap; no published result transfers the threshold to a bounded-rank causal-effect-identification design class.
proposed.consumer: Algorithm designers can treat a certified factor-two rank-three solution as worst-case optimal under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), focusing engineering effort on instance-specific improvement.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Applies the well-typed nonempty-clutter narrowing and adds the theorem-granularity Unique Games hardness leaf used by the transfer proof.

proposed.statement:
Enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three, optimize or
two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by
alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of
\(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an
exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer
costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails,
deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
proposed.justification: The interface safely exploits low rank without pretending to recognize the promise from a successful run.
proposed.gap: The WPMAX-SAT and ILP formulations of Elahi and coauthors solve unrestricted MCID but do not return a violated-rank certificate, while explicit bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume the promise externally.
proposed.consumer: RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified solution guarantee or a concrete large hedge to pass to the unrestricted backend.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declares the fixed-point oracle and the bow-free triple-structure dependencies used by the certifying interface.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether finite simple bow-free singleton ADMG rank-at-most-three recognition is polynomial-time decidable or \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-complete.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed-point oracle decides whether a specified induced vertex set contains a hedge, but neither bounded-size enumeration nor the optimizer's successful feasibility check certifies the global absence of an inclusion-minimal residual of size greater than three. The frozen core contains neither a polynomial absence certificate nor a promise-preserving reduction proving \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-hardness.
open_obligations.attempted: Alternating ancestor/district restriction and deletion minimization yield explicit large minimal hedges when one is exposed, but they do not force an exposed large hedge on every rank-violating graph without potentially exploring exponentially many deletions. The optimizer-or-violation interface can succeed globally even when another large minimal hedge exists, so success cannot be repurposed as rank recognition.
open_obligations.partial_result:
There is a polynomial verifier for the complementary language
\(r(G,s)>3\), so deciding \(r(G,s)\leq3\) belongs to \(\mathsf{coNP}\).
Indeed, a certificate is \(F=R\cup\{s\}\) with \(|R|>3\).  Verify by graph
search that \(F\) is a hedge, and for every \(v\in R\) run the fixed-point
hedge oracle on \(F\setminus\{v\}\), accepting only if it returns no hedge.
If a proper hedge \(J\subsetneq F\) existed, some
\(v\in F\setminus J\) would make \(J\subseteq F\setminus\{v\}\), a
contradiction.  Thus the certificate proves
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) and \(|R|>3\).  Conversely, the definition of rank
supplies such a certificate whenever \(r(G,s)>3\).  The certificate has
linear size and requires only polynomially many polynomial-time graph
searches.
